---
title: "Simulation (paper), step 2: generate detection counts and truths"
---

Step 2 of the paper simulation (ML design): for every dataset of step 1 and every performance variant
the slide effects and the detection counts (TP, FN, FP) of an ML model, and the true values of
recall, precision and F1 that the methods should estimate.

**Data-generating process** (`simulate_ml_dataset()`)

- Slide effects on logit recall and log FP_rate, correlated normals.
- TP ~ Bin(P, recall_slide), FN = P - TP.
- FP ~ Poisson(FP_rate_slide + fp_per_object · P): FP from look-alikes (independent of P) plus FP
  that scale with the number of objects.

**Performance variants**

| variant | scenarios | variant_name | recall | FP_rate | fp_per_object | sd recall | sd FP_rate | cor | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A-C | base | 0.8 | 2 | 0.05 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | parameters estimated from the ML model of the pathologist data |
| 2 | A-C | FP independent of P | 0.8 | 2 | 0 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | FP purely from look-alikes (no FP per object) |
| 3 | A-C | higher performance | 0.9 | 1 | 0.05 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | higher recall and precision |
| 4 | A-C | low slide heterogeneity | 0.65 | 3.1 | 0.05 | 0.3 | 0.4 | 0.7 | small slide effects, lower performance (recall as MIDOG Model 2) |
| 5 | D | D: baseline | 0.8 | 0.1 | 0 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | good detector with few FP (radiology) |
| 6 | D | D: more FP | 0.8 | 0.5 | 0 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | as 5 with 5 times more FP |
| 7 | D | D: conservative | 0.65 | 0.05 | 0 | 0.8 | 1.2 | 0.7 | conservative operating point: stricter threshold, lower recall (as variant 4 / MIDOG Model 2) and fewer FP |

sd recall, sd FP_rate: SD of the slide effects on logit recall and log FP_rate; cor: their correlation.

The FP rates of variants 1-4 (per slide, calibrated to the mitosis data) are too high for scenario D
(1.5 objects per slide on average: precision 0.2-0.4), so scenario D has its own variants with 0.1
or 0.5 FP per slide. Variant 6 changes the FP rate of variant 5; variant 7 is another operating
point on the same FROC curve (a stricter threshold lowers recall and FP together).

**Truth** (superpopulation of step 1, 10^6 slides per scenario, with its own slide effects per
variant; the same truth applies to 40 and 100 slides), from the expected counts
E[TP] = P · recall_slide, E[FP] = FP_rate_slide + fp_per_object · P:

- pooled: metrics of the summed expected counts;
- grouped: mean of the per-slide metrics.

**Seeds** (offsets from `01_seed_offsets.csv`)

- Counts of a dataset: `seed + 1000000 * variant`.
- Slide effects of the superpopulation: `seed_superpop + 1000000 * variant`.

**Output** (`simulation/data/`)

- `02_ML_performance_variants.csv`: parameters of the performance variants.
- `02_ML_performance_observed_data.csv.xz`: one row per slide, dataset and variant: `scenario`,
  `n_slide`, `rep`, `seed`, `variant`, `slide`, `P`, `TP`, `FN`, `FP`. `seed` is the dataset seed of
  step 1 (`seed_base + rep`); the later steps add their offsets from `01_seed_offsets.csv`.
- `02_truth_superpopulation.csv`: `scenario`, `variant`, `name`, `averaging`, `truth`.

```{r}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(readr)
```

# Functions
```{r}
# F1-score from the counts (paper eq. 3); defined if TP = 0 (paper "Case B": 0)
calc_F1_score <- function(TP, FP, P) {
  2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)
}

# One ML dataset on the given slides.
# recall and FP_rate refer to a slide with all slide effects = 0.
# The slide difficulty effects on logit recall and log FP_rate are correlated normals.
# TP ~ Bin(P, recall_slide), FN = P - TP
# FP ~ Poisson(FP_rate_slide + fp_per_object * P): FP from look-alikes plus FP per true object
simulate_ml_dataset <- function(
    slides, # Slide dataset with ground truth object counts
    recall, FP_rate, # Model performance
    fp_per_object, # FP per true object (0: FP independent of P)
    sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty # Slide effects
    ) {
  slides |>
    mutate(
      recall = recall,
      FP_rate = FP_rate,
      # Correlated slide effects from two independent standard normals (Cholesky)
      z_recall       = rnorm(n()),
      z_FP_rate      = rnorm(n()),
      effect_recall  = sd_slide_difficulty_recall * z_recall,
      effect_FP_rate = sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate *
        (cor_slide_difficulty * z_recall + sqrt(1 - cor_slide_difficulty^2) * z_FP_rate),
      # True recall and expected FP of this slide
      recall_slide      = plogis(qlogis(recall) + effect_recall),
      FP_rate_slide     = FP_rate * exp(effect_FP_rate),
      FP_expected_slide = FP_rate_slide + fp_per_object * P,
      # Observed counts
      TP = rbinom(n(), P, recall_slide),
      FN = P - TP,
      FP = rpois(n(), FP_expected_slide)
    ) |>
    select(slide, P, recall_slide, FP_expected_slide, TP, FN, FP)
}

# True metrics from the expected counts of each slide: E[TP] = P * recall_slide,
# E[FP] = FP_expected_slide.
#   pooled  = metric of the summed expected counts (weighted by object count)
#   grouped = mean of the per-slide metrics (each slide same weight)
calc_true_metrics <- function(df_sim) {
  df_sim |>
    mutate(TP_expected = P * recall_slide) |>
    summarise(
      Recall_pooled     = sum(TP_expected) / sum(P),
      Precision_pooled  = sum(TP_expected) / sum(TP_expected + FP_expected_slide),
      F1_pooled         = calc_F1_score(sum(TP_expected), sum(FP_expected_slide), sum(P)),
      Recall_grouped    = mean(recall_slide),
      Precision_grouped = mean(TP_expected / (TP_expected + FP_expected_slide)),
      F1_grouped        = mean(calc_F1_score(TP_expected, FP_expected_slide, P))
    ) |>
    # long format: one row per metric (name) and averaging
    pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = c("name", "averaging"), names_sep = "_",
                 values_to = "truth")
}
```

# Load slides
```{r}
df_slide_scenarios <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slide_scenarios.csv")
df_slides          <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slides.csv.xz")
df_slides_superpop <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_slides_superpop.csv.xz")
df_seed_offsets    <- read_csv("simulation/data/01_seed_offsets.csv")

offset_counts <- df_seed_offsets |> filter(step == "counts") |> pull(offset)
```

# Performance variants
```{r}
# scenario_set: the scenarios of a variant (variants 1-4: A-C, variants 5-7: D)
df_variants <- tribble(
  ~variant, ~scenario_set, ~variant_name,             ~recall, ~FP_rate, ~fp_per_object, ~sd_slide_difficulty_recall, ~sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, ~cor_slide_difficulty,
  1,        "A-C",         "base",                    0.8,     2,        0.05,           0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7,
  2,        "A-C",         "FP independent of P",     0.8,     2,        0,              0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7,
  3,        "A-C",         "higher performance",      0.9,     1,        0.05,           0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7,
  4,        "A-C",         "low slide heterogeneity", 0.65,    3.1,      0.05,           0.3,                         0.4,                         0.7,
  5,        "D",           "D: baseline",             0.8,     0.1,      0,              0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7,
  6,        "D",           "D: more FP",              0.8,     0.5,      0,              0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7,
  7,        "D",           "D: conservative",         0.65,    0.05,     0,              0.8,                         1.2,                         0.7
)

df_variants
```

# Generate counts
```{r}
# One simulation per dataset and variant of its scenario, each with its own seed
df_counts <- df_slides |>
  nest(slides = c(slide, group, P)) |>
  mutate(scenario_set = if_else(scenario == "D", "D", "A-C")) |>
  inner_join(df_variants, by = "scenario_set", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(
    seed_counts = seed + offset_counts * variant,
    sim = pmap(list(slides, seed_counts, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                    sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty),
               \(slides, seed_counts, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                 sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty) {
                 set.seed(seed_counts)
                 simulate_ml_dataset(slides, recall = recall, FP_rate = FP_rate,
                                     fp_per_object = fp_per_object,
                                     sd_slide_difficulty_recall = sd_slide_difficulty_recall,
                                     sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate = sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate,
                                     cor_slide_difficulty = cor_slide_difficulty)
               })
  ) |>
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, seed, variant, sim) |>
  unnest(sim) |>
  # Counts (without the true per-slide values)
  select(scenario, n_slide, rep, seed, variant, slide, P, TP, FN, FP)
```

# Truth
```{r}
# Superpopulation truth: superpopulation of each scenario with own slide effects per variant
df_truth_superpop <- df_slides_superpop |>
  nest(slides = c(slide, group, P)) |>
  left_join(distinct(df_slide_scenarios, scenario, seed_superpop), by = "scenario") |>
  mutate(scenario_set = if_else(scenario == "D", "D", "A-C")) |>
  inner_join(df_variants, by = "scenario_set", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(
    seed_counts = seed_superpop + offset_counts * variant,
    truth = pmap(list(slides, seed_counts, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                      sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty),
                 \(slides, seed_counts, recall, FP_rate, fp_per_object,
                   sd_slide_difficulty_recall, sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate, cor_slide_difficulty) {
                   set.seed(seed_counts)
                   simulate_ml_dataset(slides, recall = recall, FP_rate = FP_rate,
                                       fp_per_object = fp_per_object,
                                       sd_slide_difficulty_recall = sd_slide_difficulty_recall,
                                       sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate = sd_slide_difficulty_FPrate,
                                       cor_slide_difficulty = cor_slide_difficulty) |>
                     calc_true_metrics()
                 })
  ) |>
  select(scenario, variant, truth) |>
  unnest(truth)
```

# Save
```{r}
write_csv(df_variants, "simulation/data/02_ML_performance_variants.csv")
write_csv(df_counts, "simulation/data/02_ML_performance_observed_data.csv.xz")
write_csv(df_truth_superpop, "simulation/data/02_truth_superpopulation.csv")
```

# Check
```{r}
# Number of datasets per scenario, number of slides and variant
df_counts |>
  distinct(scenario, n_slide, rep, variant) |>
  count(scenario, n_slide, variant, name = "datasets")

# Superpopulation truth
df_truth_superpop |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = averaging, values_from = truth) |>
  arrange(variant, name, scenario)

# Scenario D: share of slides without detections per variant (Case B: precision and F1 = 0)
df_counts |>
  filter(scenario == "D") |>
  group_by(variant) |>
  summarise(no_detections = mean(TP + FP == 0), F1_slide = mean(2 * TP / (P + TP + FP)))
```
